second_order: making the wait for Tool news into a joke
theme_note: These passages turn expected album, song, and streaming news into bait and answers: posters announce or invent news, while replies get caught, expose the date, dismiss the effort, joke back, or call the long wait itself the joke. What varies is who starts the bait and whether the reply laughs, rejects it, or describes the hurt.

second_order: pretending r/toolband and r/tooljerk swapped places
theme_note: One exchange sustains the subreddit’s own April Fools move: the post reverses where memes and constructive content belong, borrows a moderator voice, and replies refuse, extend, and reverse the move. Its shared practice is the local swap joke, not the canvas.

second_order: calling people in and showing them how to place
theme_note: These codes recruit hands and make participation possible by asking for help, giving links, answering mobile questions, naming apps, and confirming that a contribution works. Calls vary from general rallies to practical access and color guidance.

second_order: finding and moving the Tool mark when a spot fails
theme_note: These passages choose a location, report a takeover or disappearance, call retreat, and redirect placers to replacement coordinates or plans. What varies is the obstacle—interference, a wave, scarce corner space, or a deal that is not working—and how definite the next target is.

second_order: building, correcting and holding the logo and eye
theme_note: These passages do the pixel work: starting or extending the mark, naming repairs, placing repeatedly, correcting letters, and calling people to save what is being overwritten. The work varies between construction, small corrections, and defense.

second_order: arguing over whether the pixel stuff belongs here
theme_note: These passages question, identify, dismiss, defend, or explain r/place when people object to the canvas and its posts. Positions vary from digital-diarrhea dismissal to curiosity and a defense of shared interactive art.

second_order: fitting one plan to the people and space available
theme_note: This first passage asks for agreement on a replacement plan through upvotes. Later instances extend the practice into matching design size and direction to manpower, defensible space, and a shared plan.

second_order: pointing out the screaming carrots at 235, 915
theme_note: This single code names another canvas drawing at exact coordinates. It belongs with no other practice closely enough to merge without turning a concrete pointer into a broad miscellaneous theme.

second_order: asking neighbors for space, peace and help
theme_note: These exchanges work around nearby groups by welcoming help, requesting truces or room, trading defense, promising reciprocal pixels, messaging erasers, and seeking moderators or allies. What varies is whether the neighbor begins as helper, obstacle, opponent, or negotiated partner; war words do not erase the repeated peace and help work.

second_order: celebrating, thanking and recording what they made
theme_note: These passages announce completion or success, thank builders, credit contributors, and later preserve accounts of the work. Celebration varies from brief victory posts to named thanks and careful records.

second_order: giving up sleep and time to keep the art going
theme_note: These passages organize overnight guards, wonder who is left building, remain awake near completion, or describe the work entering dreams. The commitment varies between planned coverage, isolation, exhaustion, and absorbed attention.

second_order: turning damage and rebuilding into part of the story
theme_note: These passages recount the mark being wiped out and answer loss through a lyric. Later codes extend the practice by treating last-second damage, repeated rebuilding, and imperfect survival as the account of what the group made.

second_order: bringing people into r/toolband through the canvas
theme_note: These passages show outsiders finding the subreddit through its canvas work and later credit that work with recruiting. The practice varies from a reported arrival to an explicit justification or retrospective claim.

second_order: getting back to normal Tool talk after the pixels
theme_note: These passages explicitly close the canvas episode by welcoming ordinary talk, joking that there is still no Tool news, claiming speculation as the room’s hobby, preferring it to pixel crap, or welcoming unrelated material as a change. What varies is relief, dismissal, and reuse of the older album-wait joke.
